domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's leave application. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and potential cancellation. References the employee, the leave type/policy, and the actor who performed each state-changing action.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behavior. Each leave type (annual, sick, emergency) maps to one active policy per fiscal year.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved (increment usedDays) or cancelled after approval (decrement usedDays).

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. The employee is the actor who applies for leave and the subject whose balances are tracked. The managerId field establishes the approval hierarchy — a leave request is routed to the employee's manager for approval. The role field supports RBAC enforcement (GP-005).

domain_entities.name: Notification
domain_entities.purpose: Represents a notification triggered by leave lifecycle events. Sent to employees (e.g., approval/rejection notices) and managers (e.g., new requests awaiting action). Each notification is linked to the originating leave request for traceability.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: employee, policy, audit
recommended_phases.rationale: These three modules have zero internal dependencies on other domain modules. Employee provides identity, manager relationships, and RBAC role data. Policy defines leave types, entitlements, and approval rules. Audit provides the cross-cutting audit trail required by GP-002. All three are leaf nodes in the dependency graph and must exist before any other module can be built.

sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for authentication and employee search; manager_id: frequent queries to find direct reports of a manager; role: filtering employees by role for RBAC and approval routing; employment_status: filtering active employees for leave eligibility checks

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, rejected_by, rejected_at, rejection_reason, cancelled_by, cancelled_at, cancellation_reason, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id; rejected_by -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of leave requests by employee; leave_type_id: reporting and balance calculations grouped by leave type; status: filtering by status (draft/submitted/approved/rejected/cancelled) is the most common access pattern; approved_by: managers querying their approval history; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, accrued_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup for balance queries per employee per policy per fiscal year — the dominant access pattern; employee_id: balance summary views for a single employee across all leave types; fiscal_year: annual rollover and archival queries; status: filtering by balance status (active/exhausted/frozen)

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, allow_negative_balance, max_consecutive_days, fiscal_year, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: policy lookup by leave type is the primary access pattern; fiscal_year: policies can change annually; queries scoped by year; is_active: filtering active policies for new leave requests

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: fetching notifications for a specific user is the dominant access pattern; status: filtering unread/read/archived notifications; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: looking up notifications tied to a specific leave request or other entity; created_at: chronological ordering of notification feeds

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, changed_by, old_values, new_values, created_at | pk: id | fks: changed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit trail lookups for a specific entity (e.g., all changes to a leave request); changed_by: audit queries by user who performed the action; action: filtering audit logs by action type (create/update/delete/approve/reject); created_at: time-range audit queries
